page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The CPU includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions, Advanced Vector Extensions for Vector Neural Network Instructions (AVX512_VNNI), and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested instances. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth for small cached blocks fall within the average range. A notable bottleneck exists in memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks, where both read and write speeds are weak, scoring in the bottom 25%. Similarly, while small-model LLM inference (135M parameters) performs at average speeds, medium-model (7B parameters) text generation is poor, falling into the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Given its performance profile, this instance is appropriate for web serving, database operations, software compilation, and general-purpose applications that do not rely heavily on massive uncached memory transfers or large-scale machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8 is a general-purpose server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 4 physical cores with hyper-threading and supports AVX-512 instructions. While single-core CPU performance is strong, multi-core execution and cached memory bandwidth remain average. Tradeoffs include weak uncached large-block memory bandwidth and poor performance on medium-sized LLM inference tasks. Lacking local storage and GPUs, this instance offers a balanced resource profile for standard workloads. It is best suited for static web serving, database operations, and software compilation.
